messages:
alex: Heads up — large latency spike on ephemeral NVMe in eu-west-1 GPU pool after last night's scrubber rollout. Multiple pods stuck in Init, per-GPU throughput down ~80%. Anyone else seeing this?

maria: Yep, saw it on the dashboards ~03:10 UTC. Node flapping + kubelet restarts correlated.

alex: Logs from one host show repeated controller resets and I/O timeouts:
```
[  123.456] nvme nvme0: controller reset due to error, status 0x7
[  123.457] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 8388608
[  124.120] EXT4-fs error (device nvme0n1): ext4_journal_check_start: Detected aborted journal
```

cheng: Oncall here — running nvme SMART + iostat now. Can someone run `sudo nvme list && iostat -x 1 3` on an affected host and paste output?

alex: Running it on gpu-euw-12, quick snippet:
```
# sudo nvme list
Node             SN        Model             Namespace Usage
/dev/nvme0n1     S12345    PM1735            1         99%
# iostat -x 1 3
Device: r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.0  500.0 0  102400  204.8   12.34   120.00 0.10 119.90 0.80  96.5
```

infra-bot: Alert: node gpu-euw-12 reported nvme error counter increase (controller reset) — automated alert created.

sam: My suspicion: the new ephemeral cleaner is racing with kubelet/device rename. Cleaner unmounts then rebinds NVMe namespaces -> /dev paths shift (nvme0 -> nvme1) while containers still reference old dev -> I/O errors and journal aborts. We ran into similar with nested loop devices months ago.

maria: Can we mitigate quickly by excluding NVMe devices from the cleaner's pattern? I'll push a patch to skip `/dev/nvme*` and restart the cron.

cheng: Temporary mitigation that helped: drain the newest nodes in the pool, restart kubelet on affected hosts, and revert the scrubber image. Reverted image stopped new errors within ~2 minutes. I'll open an incident ticket (INC-2026-374) and start the rollback.

alex: Confirmed rollback stops new failures. Proposed plan: rollback complete, schedule a controlled redeploy/patch tomorrow 02:00 UTC with additional safety checks (device-id pinning, udev stable names). Need a small maintenance window for nodes that need fsck.

sam: Note — one host's dmesg showed low-level bitflips before controller reset. We'll need to run `fsck -f` and nvme diagnostics on nodes that had journal aborts. Eng-sre to coordinate.

maria: Cost/impact note: degraded throughput increased GPU job duration ~30% for the affected pool during the outage window — rough cost delta +$4k/day while issue persists. Flagging finance and CS for billing/uptime impact.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook excerpt: 1) cordon node 2) `sudo nvme reset -s` on controllers 3) run `sudo fsck -y /dev/nvme0n1` if journal errors present 4) remount and `systemctl restart kubelet`. Full runbook: https://runbooks.internal/nvme-cleanup

cheng: I'll own rollback verification and postmortem. Taking this to high priority.

alex: Thanks all — creating PR for the scrubber revert and the follow-up mitigation checks. Will update incident with timeline and affected host list. :white_check_mark:
